title: dedicated-capacity-pool-wires-and-backlog
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working spec for the Dedicated Capacity management surface: the UI that lets customers create and operate GPU pools, configure autoscaling and bursts, manage reservations, and estimate cost/throughput. Focus is on: one-page pool overview, quick actions for scale/burst, reservation lifecycle, and observability hooks (latency/cost).

Audience:
- Product and UX for console
- Frontend engineers implementing routes and components
- Backend/infra owners owning pool API surfaces and billing hooks
- Solutions engineering (customer feedback loop)

High-level goals (user stories):
- As a platform engineer I can create a GPU pool with a target capacity, autoscale rules and reserve a baseline for predictable throughput.
- As an app owner I can add burst capacity for a scheduled window and get a cost estimate before applying.
- As an SRE I can see key SLOs per pool (p99 latency, queue depth, token-throughput) and attach alerts.
- As finance I can export reservations and usage to reconcile committed spend.

Top-level navigation
- Left rail: Dedicated > Pools (list) > Pool detail > Reservations > History
- Global quick action: New pool / Request burst

Page: Pool list (wireframe notes)
- List minimal card per pool: name, region, instance type(s), current nodes, expected QPS, active reservations badge, health indicator (green/yellow/red).
- Right of each row: actions: Edit, Scale now, Create reservation, View metrics
- Filter bar: region, model family, instance type, status
- Inline cost-estimate toggle: switch between "hourly cost" and "effective token cost"
- Inline bulk actions: select multiple pools -> bulk scale / export CSV

Pool detail (main wireframe)
Header area (top 160px):
- Pool name (editable inline), id, region, owner/team tag, billing contract id, status pill (Active / Draining / Idle), last modified
- Primary buttons: Edit config, Scale now, Create reservation, Start burst

Primary sections (stacked vertically, collapsible):
1) Overview row (compact):
   - Current capacity: 12 gpus (3xA100:40GB)
   - Active requests (1m/5m), queue depth, avg latency
   - Cost burn rate: $52/hr (hover => breakdown tokens/idle nodes/overprovision)
   - Utilization sparkline (1h/24h/7d controls)

2) Autoscaling rules (visual editor):
   - Compact list of rules: "Scale up: queue_depth > 12 for 30s => +2 nodes (max 20)"; "Scale down: cpu_util < 20% for 5m => -1 node"
   - Wireframe: timeline slider for cooldowns, numeric inputs, metric chooser (queue, cpu, p99 latency, token-rate)
   - Inline simulation button: "Run sim on last 24h" (opens modal with chart overlay)
   - UX note: default safeguards suggested: min_nodes, max_nodes, cool_down_ms, scale_step. Hard to edit step? default to 1/2 node increments depending on instance type.

3) Burst configuration panel (card):
   - What is a burst: temporary quota override that allocates from regional spare capacity (or queued burst request to Redwood dedicated pool).
   - Fields: start/end time (calendar + quick presets: 1h, 4h), max additional nodes, budget cap, pre-approval required toggle (for >$X).
   - Cost preview: shows estimated incremental cost and expected throughput change (tokens/s).
   - UX microcopy: "Burst uses pooled spare capacity. If region capacity is constrained, request will be queued and you’ll receive email when scheduled."
   - Action: Request burst (opens confirm modal with breakdown and snooze option)

4) Reservations (card + table):
   - Table columns: reservation id, start, end, nodes, instance_type, committed_hours, status, owner, actions (extend / cancel / convert)
   - Convert: change reservation into rolling commit (early-bird conversion to annual) — requires billing approval flow (link to billing ticket template)
   - Reservation lifecycle: Pending -> Active -> Expiring -> Draining -> Completed

5) Metrics and traces (embedded panels / linkouts):
   - Top KPI tiles: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, tail queue time, cost per 1M tokens
   - Historical chart: stacked area for active nodes vs queued requests vs bursts applied
   - Drill-in: click a spike -> open time range, show sample requests and associated model version
   - Export: CSV, Prometheus query, open in Observability console

6) Audit & Actions timeline:
   - Chronological activity (who changed autoscale rule X, who requested burst, API keys used) with filters and ability to open linked ticket

Wireframe ASCII sketch (for frontend reference):
[POOL DETAIL PAGE]
Header: [Pool name] [Active] [Edit] [Scale now] [Request burst]
Overview: [Curr cap: 12 GPU] [Q depth: 3] [Latency p99: 120ms] [Cost $52/hr]
Autoscale: [List of rules]  [Add rule +]  [Simulate]
Burst: [Start|End] [Max nodes] [Budget cap] [Request burst]
Reservations: [Table rows...]
Metrics: [KPI tiles] [Chart]
Activity: [timeline]

Micro-interactions and accessibility notes:
- Inline edits use auto-save + small toast confirming. Important edits (min/max nodes, billing changes) should show a confirm modal with an undo timer (10s) to prevent accidental changes.
- All controls keyboard accessible; charts offer CSV download and underlying datapoint table for screen readers.
- Color palette for health: green/yellow/red with text labels and icons for colorblind support

API and backend mapping (dev notes):
- Pool config GET/PUT -> /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}
- Autoscale rules stored as list of rule objects; support simulation endpoint: POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/simulate-autoscale with timeframe param
- Bursts: POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/bursts -> returns request_id, status (queued/approved/allocated)
- Reservation lifecycle endpoints: /reservations, /reservations/{id}/extend, /cancel
- Billing: any reservation or burst that changes committed hours must fire billing webhook and queue an invoice preview job (ticket linked in artifacts)

Open questions (needs quick decisions):
1) Reservation UI: Should we allow partial node reservations (e.g., fractional GPUs via time-slicing) or only whole-node? (Infra prefers integer nodes for now)
2) Burst queue UX: synchronous vs async. For now we show estimated queue position. Need product decision on SLA messaging.
3) Role-based restrictions: Should non-billing users be allowed to create reservations? Proposed: only owners + billing-admins.
4) Simulation fidelity: how accurate is "Run sim on last 24h"? Should surface confidence band.

Acceptance criteria for an MVP (QA + product):
- Create pool flow: create pool with region, instance type, min/max nodes, autoscale rule set -> pool appears in list and detail page populated
- Scale now works and changes desired nodes (reflected in API + timeline)
- Request and activate a short burst (sandbox) with cost preview and status updates (queued -> allocated -> completed)
- Reservations: create + extend + cancel flows work and map to billing preview
- Metrics tiles show consistent numbers with infra telemetry within 5%
- All critical actions require confirmation and produce an audit entry

Backlog (prioritized)
- P0: Pool create/edit, scale now, metrics tiles, audit timeline, reservation create/cancel (sprint 1)
- P1: Autoscale visual editor + simulation, basic burst request flow, role-based access controls (sprint 2)
- P2: Cost breakdown explorer, reservation conversion tools, scheduled bursts, CSV export (sprint 3)
- P3: Fractional reservation support, predictive autoscale suggestions (ML), multi-pool bulk operations (future)

Notes to engineers / implementation hints:
- Try to reuse existing KPI tile components from Hosted API (product/components/kpi-tiles).
- Autoscale rules editor can reuse the rule DSL from serving-runtime service (ask @Samir for protobuf schema).
- For simulation, use a cached 24h sample so frontend doesn't block on long-running queries; surface a job id and allow polling.

Customer examples / edge cases observed in interviews:
- Customer A (video generation startup) needs guaranteed baseline for nightly batch runs; they want a "reserve for window" that aligns with their batch schedule (support recurring reservations?)
- Customer B wants pre-approved bursts under $500 without manual billing approval
- Corner case: region capacity shortage -> bursts stay queued for >24h; need clear escalation path to sales/solutions eng

Next steps / immediate actions:
- Decision: allow fractional GPUs? (owner: Maya) -> set meeting with Infra (Diego) by 2024-11-12
- Frontend: prototype pool list + detail skeleton (owner: Hannah) -> due 2024-11-22
- Backend: instrument simulate-autoscale endpoint and reservation lifecycle (owner: Samir) -> due 2024-11-29

Changelog:
- 2024-11-05 initial draft
- 2024-11-19 added burst UX and cost preview language (Priya)
- 2024-12-02 clarified autoscale cooldown UX and default suggestions (Diego)
- 2025-01-15 updated acceptance criteria and added backlog priorities (Maya)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; feel free to add inline comments or push edits. Link to figma frames in Confluence doc referenced above.
